newsitem.title: USA: Citation sees Q4 revs lower than Q2, Q3.
newsitem.headline: Citation sees Q4 revs lower than Q2, Q3.

text.p: Citation Corp said Monday it expects fourth quarter revenues to be below those of its second and third quarters because of brief shutdowns of some of its facilities in July and August.

Citation, which supplies metal components to capital and durable goods industries, reported earnings for the third quarter ended June 29 rose to $0.44 per share from $0.39 a year earlier on sales of $177.9 million.

The company said its fiscal fourth quarter ending in September is "normally slower" than its second and third quarters because of shutdowns at its customers' facilities for model changeover and maintenance.
The company said however that it expects a positive comparison with its 1996 fourth quarter. Last year the company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.08 per share on sales of $131.6 million.
"Looking forward, our backlogs are in good shape and we continue to expect reasonably good demand for our products as long as the economy stays approximately in its current path," the company said.

"Our passenger car business appears softer than earlier in the year, although light trucks continue very strong. Our orders for heavy truck components appear somewhat stronger than last year and heavy capital goods remain strong."
